screen: Competency Management — unit cm-assess-profiles-certs: (1) Assessment & Calibration Workspace, (2) Employee Competency Profile, (3) Certification & Compliance Center
screenLevelGaps: ASSESSMENTS CANNOT GROW A KASBA LEVEL — THE WRITE PATH DOES NOT EXIST, AND NEITHER DOES THE RATING CAPTURE. Traced end to end: (a) s_competency_assessments (migration 2026_07_28_100100_create_competency_module_tables.php:79-100) has ONE aggregate column `score decimal(5,2)` and NO per-competency / per-KASBA-dimension child table — there is nowhere to record 'Java: knowledge 3, ability 2'. (b) The only writes to that table in the entire backend are AssessmentController::store (insert, status defaults 'open'), AssessmentController::destroy (soft delete) and AssessmentCycleController::reviewAssessment (sets review_status only). Nothing anywhere sets status='completed', score, or completed_at. (c) grep for s_skill_matrix writes across app/ returns exactly two call sites, both in EmployeeCompetencyProfileController (insertGetId L272, update L351) — i.e. the two manual admin buttons on the Employee Profile screen. No assessment code path, and no LMS code path, touches s_skill_matrix. CONCLUSION: an assessment is a bare envelope (title, user, jobrole, due date, status). It captures no ratings, produces no score, and can never move a level in s_skill_matrix. The KASBA level only ever changes when a human clicks 'Add Competency' or 'Update Rating' on the Employee Profile screen.

ASSESSMENTS ARE NOT CONNECTED TO LMS IN EITHER DIRECTION. No file under app/Http/Controllers/Api/Competency/ references lms_certificates, lms_course_enroll or sub_std_map except DevelopmentPlanController and LearningAssignmentController (which read lms_assignments). The Assessment Workspace has no course-recommendation surface, no 'assign learning from this gap' action, and no ingestion of course completion. Per the ownership model (Competency=measure, LMS=build), a completed assessment should emit a gap set that LMS turns into a targeted training plan, and a completed course should feed evidence back into the measured level. Neither edge exists.

THE WHOLE ASSESSMENT LIFECYCLE IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE UI, SO EVERY DOWNSTREAM KPI IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO. There is no self-assessment form, no manager rating form and no score entry anywhere in the product. Because nothing can set status='completed', 'Overall Completion' is permanently 0%, 'Pending Manager Ratings' (completed AND review_status IS NULL) is permanently 0, the Approvals tab is permanently empty, and the Score column always renders '—'. review_status='pending_review' is written by exactly one branch — action='reject' in AssessmentCycleController::reviewAssessment:367 — and the UI never sends 'reject' (cm-assessment-workspace.tsx:585 sends only 'calibrate' or 'approve'), so the Calibration tab can never populate either. The four KPI tiles and three of the five top tabs are dead by construction.

SEVEN LIVE BACKEND ENDPOINTS FOR THIS SCREEN HAVE NO FRONTEND CALLER AT ALL. routes/api.php:335-343 expose GET/PUT /competency/assessment-cycles/configuration, GET /{id}, PUT /{id}, GET /{id}/ratings, GET /{id}/calibration-queue, GET /{id}/audit-trail — all fully implemented in AssessmentCycleController (L518-1039, ~520 lines including score buckets, department split, target-threshold comparison and a real audit feed). services/competency/assessment-workspace.ts declares NONE of them. The UI instead renders 'This section is coming soon' for the Overview / Ratings / Calibration / Audit Trail campaign tabs (cm-assessment-workspace.tsx:468-471) and leaves 'View Configuration', 'View Details' and 'Edit Campaign' as onClick-less buttons. This is finished backend work orphaned by a missing 8-line service file.

CUSTOMER'S 'ONLY ONE PROFILE' REPORT IS CONFIRMED, AND THE CAUSE IS EXACT. CmEmployeeProfiles takes an optional `userId` prop (cm-employee-profiles.tsx:54) and falls back to `user?.id` (L70). hooks/content-map-m2.ts:30 mounts it as a bare component reference with NO props, and grep shows no other render site in the repo. So the screen is hardwired to the signed-in user. There is no employee list, no employee search, no employee picker and no roster route anywhere on this screen — despite the title 'Employee Competency Profile', the description 'for the employee', and the fact that the backend endpoint GET /competency/employee-profiles/{id} accepts any user id. For an HR Manager the screen is unusable: it shows their own ratings only.

THE DRILL-THROUGH INTO EMPLOYEE PROFILES IS DOUBLY BROKEN. cm-competency-library.tsx:1294 renders an 'Employees Rated' tile that calls openInSubmodule('cm-employee-profiles', item), which pushes ?competency_id=&competency= (L795-798). CmEmployeeProfiles never imports useCompetencyFocus and never reads searchParams, so the competency filter is silently dropped — and because of the previous gap, the destination shows the clicking user's own profile rather than the N employees rated on that competency. CmCertifications does read the focus correctly (cm-certifications.tsx:735, 762), which proves the pattern was known and just not applied here.

REQUIRED LEVEL AND GAP ARE STRUCTURALLY ALWAYS ZERO ON THIS TENANT. EmployeeCompetencyProfileController::show resolves the job role from tbluser.jobtitle_id (L51-57) and only then loads required levels from s_user_skill_jobrole (L82-89). PerformanceCycleController.php:434-439 documents, from a live DB check, that 'tbluser.jobtitle_id is 0 for every employee'. So $jobRoleName is 'N/A', $requiredSkills is empty, every item gets required=0 and gap = current - 0 = current. The 'Required' column, the 'Gap' column, the green/red gap colouring, the Details dialog's Required/Gap tiles and the 'Exceeds / Needs Improvement / On Target' verdict are therefore all meaningless — every competency reads as 'Exceeds'. Note the sibling method careerPath (L708-722) DOES implement a fallback (derive the role from the latest assessment); show() does not.

THE 'COMPETENCY HISTORY' TAB IS NOT HISTORY, AND NEITHER IS THE HISTORY DIALOG. competencyTimeline (cm-employee-profiles.tsx:226-234) flattens data.competencies — the CURRENT rating of each skill — and sorts by updated_at. Each competency appears exactly once, at today's level. Nothing shows a level moving over time. The per-skill History dialog is worse: EmployeeCompetencyProfileController::skillHistory:431-444 fabricates a two-entry timeline ('Current Rating' and 'Initial Assessment') that reports THE SAME skill_level for both, differing only in date. The controller admits it at L389: 'Since we don't have a dedicated history table'. The HR-Manager spec requirement 'Employee competency growth history across tenure' is therefore unmet, and s_skill_matrix has no versioning to build it from.

MUTATION BUTTONS ARE SHOWN TO USERS WHO CANNOT USE THEM. routes/api.php gates addSkill, updateSkill, saveNotes, storeEvidence and deleteEvidence behind middleware('profile:admin,hr,manager') (L347-348, 351, 355-356), but GET /competency/employee-profiles/{id} is ungated. Since the screen always renders the signed-in user's own profile, a plain employee sees 'Add Competency', 'Update Rating', the Notes pencil and 'Add Evidence' and gets a 403 on click. No role check exists in the component.

CUSTOMER'S 'CERTIFICATIONS CONNECTS TO NOTHING' IS PARTLY WRONG AND SHOULD BE CORRECTED. The screen is NOT an island inside Competency: (a) s_competency_certifications.competency_id joins to s_users_skills and is surfaced as 'Linked Competency' (CertificationController::show:330-332) and as a filter (filteredQuery:1140-1142); (b) the Competency Library's 'Certifications' count drills through into it via ?competency_id (cm-competency-library.tsx:1296 + cm-certifications.tsx:762); (c) certification documents are stored on the SHARED s_competency_evidence table (CertificationController::EVIDENCE const L34, storeDocument:1016), so an attached certificate really is competency evidence; (d) the same rows render in the Employee Profile's Certifications tab (EmployeeCompetencyProfileController::certifications:535). The 'connects to nothing' claim is only true for the three EXTERNAL edges, listed next.

CERTIFICATIONS ↔ LMS IS COMPLETELY DISCONNECTED, EVEN THOUGH THE JOIN KEY ALREADY EXISTS. LMS issues real certificates into lms_certificates (LmsLearningController:1455) and stamps each one with skill_id via resolveCourseSkillId (L965-984), which resolves to an s_users_skills row — the SAME identifier space as s_competency_certifications.competency_id and s_skill_matrix.skill_id. Despite that, grep shows lms_certificates is referenced only inside LmsLearningController; no Competency controller reads it, and CertificationController never writes one. Consequence: an employee who completes an LMS course and earns a certificate appears with ZERO certifications on the Certification & Compliance Center, and can be flagged Non-Compliant against a requirement the LMS certificate already satisfies. The two 'certification' worlds are entirely parallel (hooks/use-certifications.ts even holds both useCertifications and useLmsCertifications in one file, wired to different screens).

CERTIFICATIONS FEED NOTHING IN TALENT OR TASK MANAGEMENT. grep -rln s_competency_certifications across app/ returns only CertificationController, CertificationRequirementController, EmployeeCompetencyProfileController, skillLibraryController (legacy web), the Eloquent model, and CommandCenterService — all Competency. No file under app/Http/Controllers/Api/Talent/, /Mobility/, /Onboarding/, /Offboarding/, /Performance/ or TaskController.php contains the string 'certificat'. So a mandatory-credential gap never blocks an internal job application, never appears in succession readiness, never gates onboarding clearance, and never gates task assignment — all of which the ownership model puts squarely in Talent/Task.

VERIFYING A CERTIFICATION DOES NOT MOVE THE COMPETENCY IT IS LINKED TO. CertificationController::update (L466-488) writes only certification columns plus verified_by/verified_at. Even when competency_id is set and verification_status becomes 'verified', nothing is written to s_skill_matrix and no evidence row is auto-created against that competency. Under the ownership model a verified credential is the strongest possible proof point for a measured level; here it is inert metadata.

CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS ARE KEYED ON A FREE-TEXT JOB ROLE. RequirementDialog's 'Job Role' field is a plain <Input> (cm-certifications.tsx:430-432) with the hint 'Leave blank for all roles', while Department is a proper <Select> bound to server options. CertificationController::requirementsFor:1353-1376 then matches that string against the employee's derived jobrole. Organization/HRIT owns the job-role master (s_user_jobrole, 2,875 rows) and is already queried by CertificationController::filters:244 for role names — so a typo silently makes a mandatory compliance requirement apply to nobody, with no error.

STATUS BADGES ON TWO OF THE THREE SCREENS ARE MIS-COLOURED BECAUSE DESIGN-SYSTEM VARIANT NAMES ARE PASSED INTO THE `status` PROP. StatusBadge resolves colour as statusVariantMap[status] || variant || 'default' (components/ui/status-badge.tsx:140). The map contains no 'success', 'warning', 'info' or 'valid' keys. cm-assessment-workspace.tsx:297/357 pass status='success'|'info'; cm-employee-profiles.tsx:302/514/546/574/637/686/742 pass status='success'|'warning'|'valid'|'expiring'. All of those render grey/default. cm-certifications.tsx does it correctly with variant={...} throughout — so the two other screens are simply wrong. Related dead code: certStatusVariant is defined at cm-employee-profiles.tsx:236-240 and never called.

TWO INDEPENDENT 'ADD CERTIFICATION' FORMS WRITE THE SAME TABLE WITH DIFFERENT FIELD SETS. The Employee Profile quick action posts name / user_id / jobrole / issuing_body / issued_date / expiry_date to POST /competency/certifications (services/competency/employee-profiles.ts:223-231), silently omitting certification_type, credential_id, competency_id, requirement_id and department_id — the exact columns the Compliance Center's requirement matcher, Linked Competency field and Department filter depend on. A credential entered from the profile screen can therefore never be matched to a requirement and always shows 'Not tied to a certification requirement'.
